title: Adaptive batcher scheduler tuning for heterogeneous prompt/response lengths
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Our continuous batching scheduler currently targets throughput by grouping requests primarily by queue arrival time and max sequence length estimates. In mixed workloads where short prompts with long generations coexist with long prompts with short responses, we see suboptimal GPU utilization, elevated per-request latency variance (P95), and increased KV cache pressure leading to periodic OOMs on p4d and A100 pools. Goal: Design and implement scheduler heuristics and KV cache eviction/placement changes that reduce tail latency and OOM frequency while preserving or improving aggregate throughput. Success metrics: reduce P95 latency for interactive webhooks by >=20%, decrease OOM incidents in dedicated pools by >=80%, and maintain or increase tokens/sec throughput within 5% of baseline on representative traffic mixes.
approach: 1) Scheduler changes: introduce adaptive length-aware bucketing with soft boundaries, a token-budget-aware packer that limits per-batch token variance, and a dynamic merge/split policy for batches when short-response flows would otherwise block long-response requests. Implement per-device active_token_limit to avoid cross-request starvation and allow opportunistic small-batch fast-paths. 2) KV cache management: add a two-tier eviction policy that prefers evicting long-context KV shards for cold keys, support pinning hot short-prefix KVs for low-latency routes (console, embeddings fallback), and implement a predictive prefetch for imminent continuation requests based on recent session activity. 3) GPU memory optimization: reduce peak workspace by reusing attention scratch buffers for compatible kernels, enable fused allocator for recurrent allocations, and add a soft offload to host for very large KV shards with a predictive warm path to avoid stalls. 4) Telemetry and feature flags: expose per-batch stats (tokens, seq_len_stddev, KV_hits, memory_headroom) and gate new heuristics behind runtime feature flags for canary rollouts.
proposed_changes:
- New scheduler: adaptive_length_buckets + token_budget_packer (configurable thresholds)
- KV cache: eviction_policy=v2 with pinlist API, predictive_prefetch=true
- Memory: fused_workspace_allocator=true, kv_host_offload_threshold_tokens=20000
- Metrics: batch_length_stddev, kv_evictions/sec, device_memory_headroom_gb
- Config: per-customer overrides for latency-sensitive routes (min_batch_size=1, max_token_budget=512)
experiments: Planned experiments: A) Synthetic mixed workload (50% short prompts, long responses; 50% long prompts short responses) on dedicated staging cluster to validate P95 and OOM changes. B) Canary on 5% of production traffic for a single low-risk tenant with telemetry collection. C) Stress test on worst-case long-context traces from customer replay (internal replay bucket replay-2026-02). Metrics to collect: P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, batch_size_distribution, KV_hit_rate, OOM_count, GPU_utilization, PCIe transfer stalls.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge scheduler and KV V2 behind feature flag. 2) Run experiment A for 72 hours, iterate thresholds. 3) Canary deploy to 5% production for 48 hours with automated rollback conditions (OOM_count > 3/hr, P95 increase > 10%). 4) Increment to 25% and then full rollout with 24-hour monitoring windows. 5) Post-rollout: mark as default and add to runtime-1.22 release notes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive pinning of KVs could increase memory pressure and cause OOMs. Mitigation: conservative default pinlist size and an adaptive pin backoff when memory_headroom < 2GB. Risk: Token-budget packing could increase latency for individual long-response requests. Mitigation: allow route-level overrides and emergency bypass to legacy packer for SLAs. Risk: Host offload introduces PCIe stalls. Mitigation: predictive warm path and threshold tuned by experiments; fallback to local-only allocation if transfer latency exceeds 10ms.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add Grafana panels: 'adaptive_batcher/latency_by_route', 'kv_cache/evictions', 'device/memory_headroom', and an alert: 'KV_OOM_Rate > 0' to pager rotation. Define SLO check: rolling 24h P95 for interactive routes must not regress > 8% post-rollout.
